title: Vittorio Colao defends copyright rules and the DSA in Europe’s AI debate
summary:
Regulation is holding back AI in Europe, but not every rule in the same way, Vittorio Colao said.
Intellectual property and the value of creative work need protecting, he said.
“So when AI companies complain about copyright laws, I say, you see, sorry guys, you want me to allow stealing?” Colao said.
“Good intentions, too complicated to implement, and now we are not capable of implementing it,” Colao said of the AI Act.
Four risks to work onBeyond the debate over extinction, Colao named four AI risks: jobs and social impact, people’s judgement, wealth concentration and cybersecurity.

title: EU’s cyber agency and research centre are testing Chinese AI models
summary:
The EU’s cyber agency, ENISA, and the Commission’s own science service, the Joint Research Centre, have started testing open AI models from China, Politico reported.
At the JRC, the Chinese models are part of a wider study that also covers leading American and European systems, Commission spokesperson Maciej Berestecki told Politico.
ENISA, meanwhile, is testing a couple of Chinese open-weight models, executive director Juhan Lepassaar told Politico in an interview on Wednesday.
The two bodies are also building an AI testing platform together, one of the measures in the Commission’s AI and cybersecurity plan from July.
Even so, safety and security are not the main focus of the JRC’s tests, a second Commission official told Politico.

title: Commentator Katie Zacharia picked as new White House press secretary
summary:
Zacharia thanked him in a post on X, writing: "Serving President Trump and the American people at this critical 250-year mark is the honor of a lifetime."
She said Trump had "shown America that we can be great again, and he works to effectuate that greatness every single day".
She said she looked forward "to working with the White House press corps, and with reporters across the country, to get that record out".
Earlier this year, Zacharia wrote an op-ed in the New York Post about an incident in which she was asked to stop wearing a "Make America Great Again" hat to her local gym.
A lawyer educated at Pepperdine University in California, Zacharia also served as general counsel for Fix California, a conservative non-profit started by Trump ally - and current Special Presidential Envoy for Special Missions - Ric Grenell.

title: King Charles warns malicious online actors are evolving their tactics
summary:
King Charles III has warned of the challenges disinformation and other "hostile online activity" pose to trust and security in the digital age.
The comments, made in a letter to the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) to mark its 10th anniversary, spoke of "malicious actors" continuing to "evolve their tactics by using automated technologies".
"From threats to our international order, to the need to balance the risks and opportunities of powerful new technologies, strong cyber security is fundamental to making the online environment safer and more resilient," he wrote.
Last month, the King warned AI executives of the "existential dangers" posed by the technology falling into the wrong hands.
In the letter published on Saturday by NCSC, the King praised the government agency.

title: If the Strait of Hormuz is open, why are gas and diesel so expensive?
summary:
New York —The Strait of Hormuz is no longer paralyzed and yet fuel prices remain painfully high.
Unblocking the Strait of Hormuz has been helpful, but it’s still incredibly dangerous – and thus expensive.
‘Insane’ cost of oil supertankersThe security challenges have been underscored by the staggering cost of getting crude oil out of the Middle East.
Multiple commercial vessels reported getting struck by projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz in recent days alone, including at least two crude oil tankers, according to the United Kingdom’s Maritime Trade Operations.
Oil producers are now paying between $30 million and $40 million for a round-trip voyage in and out of the Strait of Hormuz, the Journal reported.

title: A 9-billion-year-old signal could help explain dark energy
summary:
By measuring that large-scale structure, astronomers can reconstruct how the universe expanded over time and use those measurements to investigate dark energy.
Until now, CHIME researchers needed to compare their radio observations with galaxy survey data collected by other telescopes.
What the Hydrogen Signal RevealsIn an accompanying paper, the researchers analyzed what the newly detected signal can tell scientists about how hydrogen was distributed throughout the universe.
Researchers had to use new data processing and analysis methods to extract the extremely weak hydrogen signal from much stronger sources of interference.
Their analysis ultimately showed that the signal came from hydrogen in the distant universe when the universe was about five billion years old.

title: Eritrea urges UN to intervene in standoff with Ethiopia
summary:
Share Eritrea urges UN to intervene in standoff with Ethiopia on social mediaEritrea has asked the United Nations to take “deterrent measures” after what it called Ethiopia’s “declaration of war” in the conflict over the Tigray region.
The neighbouring countries have accused each other of starting a war over Tigray, where Ethiopia says Eritrea is backing rebels.
Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos on Friday accused Eritrea of “a blatant act of aggression that engages Ethiopia’s inherent right to self-defence”.
Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel accused Ethiopia on Friday of pursuing aggression against Eritrea through its demands for sovereign access to the Red Sea.
Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993, and they fought a deadly border war from 1998 to 2000.

title: Putin tells Trump peace talks are unlikely, cites Ukraine drone attacks
summary:
Negotiators aim to present a proposal to Russia in the coming weeks, meanwhile Putin says resumption of talks unlikely.
Russian President Vladimir Putin has said an immediate resumption of peace talks with Ukraine is unlikely, citing drone attacks on Moscow during parliamentary elections last month.
In a phone call with US President Donald Trump on Friday, Putin said Moscow was ready to resume negotiations with Kyiv after the parliamentary elections.
However, the drone attacks on the capital made the resumption of trilateral peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US unlikely.
“As the president said, we will now assess when these negotiations can resume,” he added regarding the trilateral talks.

title: What we talk about when we talk about US strategic ‘credibility’ – from Vietnam to Iran
summary:
Either way, most observers insist that for the United States, “credibility is on the line in Iran.” But that has long been a central concern of U.S. foreign policy.
Historical examples are useful here, in particular the Vietnam War, during which American credibility was at stake in unprecedented ways.
Yet policymakers repeatedly insisted that Vietnam was the place where American credibility had to be demonstrated and established.
Counterintuitively, while the Vietnam War was fought in the eyes of many policymakers to defend U.S. credibility, its conclusion shattered conventional notions of credibility.
But the problem, as it was in the Vietnam War, is that credibly engaging in war and violence is not a substitute for strategy.
